leads.title: Fairness for All Marylanders Act of 2014
leads.documents: Statewide anti-discrimination protection based on gender identity; added gender identity to Maryland anti-discrimination law (sexual orientation protected since 2001).
leads.detail: No URL visible in text. Cited as: introduced Jan 2013, passed Senate 32-15 on March 4 2014, House 82-57 on March 27 2014, signed May 15 2014 by Gov. Martin O'Malley, effective Oct 1 2014; referendum petition failed.

leads.title: Maryland Transgender Sanctuary Law - 2024 Act declaring Maryland a sanctuary state
leads.documents: Openly declares Maryland a 'sanctuary state for protecting and defending transgender individuals.'
leads.detail: No URL visible. Cited as: passed Senate 33-13 in March 2024, passed House 97-38, signed by Gov. Wes Moore, effective Oct 1 2024.

leads.title: Governor Executive Order June 2023 + Medicaid gender-affirming care law effective Jan 1, 2024
leads.documents: Executive order 'protects, shields and defends' transgender individuals seeking gender-affirming healthcare; state insurance/Medicaid law described as 'most transgender healthcare friendly policies within the United States.' Separate Medicaid bill explicitly includes sexual reassignment surgery for eligible residents over 18.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Cited as: executive order signed June 2023; Medicaid bill passed both houses March 2023, signed April 2023, effective Jan 1 2024.

leads.title: HB231 - Abolition of gay or trans panic defense (2021)
leads.documents: Abolishes common-law gay or trans panic defense; amends hate-crime / criminal defense machinery.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Cited as: passed House 136-0 and Senate 47-0 in April 2021, Gov. Larry Hogan took no action, effective Oct 1 2021.

leads.title: U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland - Talbot County Public Schools ruling, March 2018
leads.documents: Ruled federal and state law protect transgender students' rights to 'use the restroom and locker rooms in alignment with their gender identity,' striking down Talbot County Public Schools policy.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Cited as March 2018 ruling of United States District Court for the District of Maryland.

leads.title: Montgomery County gender-neutral bathroom ordinance - July 2022
leads.documents: Legally allows, recognizes and implements gender-neutral bathrooms in Montgomery County; Baltimore city noted to have similar ordinance.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Cited as: approved 9-0 by Montgomery County council in July 2022.

leads.title: HB39 (2021) - Repeal of 1971 newspaper publication requirement for name change + correction of 2002 hate crime law
leads.documents: Repeals archaic 1971 law requiring individuals to publish names in newspaper before legal name change on birth certificate (privacy breach); corrects 2002 hate crime law to include 'gender identity' as separate category instead of under sexual orientation.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Cited as: two bills passed April 2021, Gov. Larry Hogan took no action, effective Oct 1 2021.

leads.title: Maryland birth certificate reform (2015) and MVA X-marker law (2019)
leads.documents: Makes it easier for transgender people to change gender marker on birth certificates without surgery/sterilization on provider certification; allows 'X' marker on Motor Vehicle Administration IDs without legal/medical documentation and on voter registration.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Cited as: 2015 law effective Oct 1 2015 (Hogan no signature); 2019 law effective Oct 1 2019 (Hogan no action); gender X still not available on birth certificates as of 2023.

leads.title: Montgomery County Office of Legislative Oversight report - February 2022
leads.documents: Government report noting gender non-conforming and transgender athletes can participate in Maryland in accordance with gender identity 'without requiring proof, documentation, or medical or legal transition' and participation is not tracked.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Cited as: report by Montgomery County Office of Legislative Oversight, February 2022.

leads.title: July 2021 police raids under Unnatural or Perverted Sexual Practices Act + repeal history
leads.documents: Documented enforcement incident: several men arrested for gay sex but not heterosexual sex under still-on-books law; documents incomplete 2020 repeal (anal repealed, oral left intact) and final repeal.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Cited as: July 2021 raids; 2020 repeal effective Oct 1 2020; June 2022 repeal bill died in Senate Judicial Proceedings Committee (Chair Sen. William C. Smith Jr., sponsor Sen. Clarence Lam); May 2023 bill became law without Governor signature, effective Oct 1 2023.
